title: Applications
text: Applications are complete, focused solutions — not general purpose toolkits — that open their own interface inside Elitea once configured. Today's catalogue has two: DeepWiki (wikis) and Inventory. See DeepWiki and Inventory for what each one does. Applications and App Catalog tabs The Applications tab lists instances already configured in the current project, in card or table view, filterable by type and pinnable for quick access. The App Catalog tab shows every application type available on the platform, each tagged Available , Configured , or By request . Configure an application Open App Catalog and find the application you want. Select Configure — shown only when your project already has access. For DeepWiki: a code toolkit, an LLM model, a max token budget, and an embedding model. For Inventory: one or more repository toolkits and the AI model settings. Select Save . The new instance appears on the Applications tab; open it to reach its interface. Request access If a catalog card shows By request , select Request Access , describe your use case, and submit. The card then shows Pending approval until an administrator reviews the request through App requests. Troubleshooting Your project has not been granted access to that application type yet — submit a request first. Confirm its underlying toolkit (the repository toolkit for DeepWiki or Inventory) still has valid credentials. DeepWiki and Inventory · Toolkits

title: Artifacts
text: Artifacts are project scoped, bucket organized file storage that agents, pipelines, and conversations read from and write to. Chat attachments and generated images land here automatically in a default attachments bucket; you can also create buckets of your own. Create a bucket 1. Select + Create Bucket . 2. Enter a Name (starts with a letter; letters, numbers, and hyphens only; 56 characters max). 3. Select Save . Creating a bucket does not set a retention period — that is configured separately, after the bucket exists. Retention Open a bucket's edit view to set a retention period in whole days. Leave it empty to keep files indefinitely; set it and files older than that many days become eligible for automatic deletion, which cannot be undone. Upload, preview, and manage files Upload by dragging files onto the file table, using the upload button, or from a bucket's context menu. Select a file's view/edit icon to preview it — code, Markdown, MDX, CSV/TSV, Mermaid, images, and DOCX all render with type appropriate views, and most can be edited in place and saved back (files over 2 MB cannot be previewed or edited). Download a single file or select several and download them together as a ZIP. Deleting all files in a folder removes the folder too — empty folders are not supported. Editing an artifact file is last save wins. If two people edit the same file at once, the later save overwrites the earlier one. Manage bucket access In team and public projects, open a bucket's Manage permissions action to set per user exceptions to the default read/write access: Read only or No access for one or more users. Selecting the default read/write option in an edit removes the exception. This is not available in personal projects. Retention notifications When a bucket's retention period is about to delete files, the bucket's owner gets a notification 24 hours ahead so there is time to back up anything still needed. See Notifications. Use a bucket from an agent or pipeline Attach the built in Artifact toolkit type to an agent or pipeline to let it read and write files in a bucket during a run — useful for a workflow that produces a report, or one that reads reference material uploaded ahead of time. An Artifact toolkit is also index capable, so an agent can search across everything in a bucket instead of reading one file at a time. See Indexing overview. Troubleshooting Confirm a bucket or folder is selected and that you hold the artifacts create permission. Check the name follows the naming rules — it must start with a letter and use only letters, numbers, and hyphens. Its bucket's retention period may have expired, or another user or an agent with Artifact toolkit access may have removed it — check the bucket's retention setting and project activity. Attach files · Data analysis · Notifications

title: Catalog
text: Catalog is the shared library of published agents and skills, visible across every project you have access to — a discovery surface, not a personal workspace. Reach it from the Catalog button near the bottom of the sidebar. Agents and Skills tabs Agents — published agents shown as cards with creator, likes, and a Start chat action. Select a card to view its full description, instructions (read only), welcome message, and conversation starters. Skills — published skills you can review and attach to one or more of your own agents with Add or Add & Test (the latter also opens a chat with the agent you attached it to). Filter either tab by category (Trending, My liked, Development, DevOps, and more) or search by name and description. Start a conversation from Catalog Select Start chat on an agent, or one of its conversation starters, to create a new conversation with that agent already active and its participant added. What you can and cannot change Published items are read only. In a conversation with a published agent you can change the model , its settings (Creativity or Reasoning Effort, Max Completion Tokens, Steps Limit), and the values of any variables it defines — these changes apply only to your conversation. You cannot edit its name, instructions, welcome message, conversation starters, or attached toolkits; to get an editable copy, fork it or build your own from the Agents menu. Troubleshooting It may not be published yet, still pending moderation, or filtered out by an active search or category filter. Refresh the page and confirm you still have Chat access; if the problem persists, contact your administrator. Agents · Skills · Use public items from chat · Agent publishing

title: Chat
text: Chat is the central place where Elitea's capabilities come together. Each conversation is an independent session — you can reference earlier messages in the same conversation, but context is not shared between separate conversations. Conversations are stored on the server and accessible from any device. Create a conversation 1. Go to Chat in the sidebar. 2. Select + Conversation , or start typing in the welcome screen's input. 3. Optionally add participants first — select + in the input toolbar, or type to search. 4. Type your message and send it. The conversation name is generated automatically from the message content. Conversations in the sidebar are grouped by Today , Yesterday , This Week , and Older ; pinned conversations always sit at the top. Folders Select the folder icon in the conversations header to create a folder, then drag conversations into it or use Move to from a conversation's context menu. In a personal project, folders and their contents are visible only to you. In a team project, folders can be shared with the whole project and cannot be converted back to private. Participants Participants extend what a conversation can do: A language model you talk to directly. Existing agents or pipelines from your project or the public catalog. Integrations already configured in the project, targetable directly with / . Connected MCP servers that expose additional tools. In team projects, teammates you can mention with @username . To add a participant, select + in the input toolbar and browse by category, or type followed by a name to search across agents, pipelines, toolkits, and MCPs. Added participants appear in the Participants panel on the right, grouped by type; select an agent or pipeline card to make it the active participant. Hovering an existing participant's card reveals an edit icon that opens its inline editor (the same form as its own menu page) without leaving the conversation. Adding an existing agent, pipeline, toolkit, or MCP to a conversation works today. Creating a brand new one from the chat + menu does not yet reach a working editor (tracked in 867). Create new entities from their own menu — Agents, Pipelines, Toolkits — then add them to the conversation. Mention a toolkit or tool Type / to search toolkits and MCPs already added to the conversation, then / again after a toolkit name to filter its individual tools. The result is inserted as /ToolkitName/ToolName , directing the AI to use that specific tool. Modules Chat supports several built in modules — image creation, data analysis, planner, smart tools selection, swarm mode, and the platform's own MCP tools — turned on from + → Modules . All of them require the Python worker; see Internal tools for what each one does and which worker runs it. File attachments Select + → Attach Files , drag files onto the input, or paste from the clipboard. Images go straight to the model for visual analysis; other files are indexed and retrieved by semantic search. Files land in the project's default attachments artifact bucket automatically — no manual toolkit setup is required. Direct model chats always allow attachments; an agent or pipeline needs attachments turned on in its own configuration first. Choose a model and settings Select the model chip at the bottom of the chat to pick a model, and the settings gear next to it to adjust generation parameters. Reasoning capable models expose a Reasoning level (Low/Medium/High); standard models expose Creativity (1–5). All models let you set Max Completion Tokens (Auto or a custom value), and conversations additionally expose a Steps Limit capping how many tool calls a turn can make (default 25). Voice Dictate into the input; transcribed text lands at the cursor. Have a response read aloud from a mini player in the input area. A hands free loop: record, send, listen to the reply, record again. Voice input uses a server side speech recognition model when your project has one configured (Settings › AI Providers), falling back to the browser's Web Speech API; text to speech works the same way with a server TTS model or the browser's speech synthesis as a fallback. Voice settings (voice, speed, volume) are saved per browser and can also be set as your default in Settings › Personal Settings. Context budget When context management is turned on for the project (Settings › Memory), a Context Budget widget appears after your first message, showing token usage and letting you trigger manual pruning or review the active summarization settings. Share a conversation Open a conversation's context menu and select Share by link to open the share dialog. Choose a link expiry (1 hour, 1 day, 7 days, or 30 days — there is no non expiring option) and, optionally, a password of at least 8 characters. The link is shown once, at creation, and copied to your clipboard automatically; it cannot be retrieved again later — if you lose it, revoke it and create a new one. Anyone who opens the link sees the conversation as it stood at share time in a read only, anonymous viewer — they can reply to nothing and add no participants — prompted for the password first if one was set. An invalid, revoked, or expired link all show the same "unavailable" message by design, so a visitor cannot tell which case applies. Sensitive action authorization When an agent or pipeline is about to call a tool your administrator has marked sensitive, the conversation pauses and shows an authorization card with the action and its parameters (secrets masked) before anything executes. See Sensitive action authorization guardrail. Canvas When a response contains code, a table, or a Mermaid diagram, a pencil icon opens it in Canvas for direct, real time collaborative editing. See How to use Canvas. Canvas edits only the block generated in the current turn — it cannot open or save a file already stored elsewhere (tracked in 878). Troubleshooting Confirm the agent, pipeline, toolkit, or MCP exists and is accessible to you in the current project. Attachments are always on for a direct model chat, but need to be turned on in the agent's or pipeline's own configuration first. No server side voice model is configured and your browser does not support the Web Speech API. Ask your administrator to configure one in AI Providers. The link may be expired, revoked, or never valid — Elitea shows the same message in every case to avoid confirming which. Attach files · Context management · Add teammates to a conversation

title: Credentials
text: A credential holds the authentication information — API key, token, username/password, or similar — a toolkit or AI provider needs to connect to an external service. Storing credentials centrally means you configure them once and reuse them across multiple toolkits and agents. Create a credential Select + Create from the Credentials page. Choose a credential type from the categorized list (code repositories, project management, testing, and more — matching the toolkit catalogue). Enter Display Name , a unique ID , and the type's specific fields — a URL, a username, and a key or token. Where offered, select Test Connection to verify the values before saving. Select Save . When a field accepts a secret, use Settings › Secrets instead of typing the value directly — the field's dropdown lets you create a new project or private secret inline. Project vs. private credentials A credential can be shared with the team (visible to any project member configuring a toolkit) or kept private to you. Team shared toolkits sometimes require each member to hold a matching private credential — see the shared credential note on the Toolkits page. Edit or delete a credential Open a credential from the dashboard to update its name or parameters and select Save , or use the delete action and confirm by typing its name. Deleting a credential in use will break the toolkit or agent that depends on it. Assign a credential When creating or editing a toolkit or an AI provider configuration, open its Credentials dropdown and select an existing credential, or create one inline. Troubleshooting Check that the key, token, or password is correct, current, and free of stray whitespace, and that your account still has access to the target service. Confirm you are viewing the right project, and that the credential has not been deleted by another team member. How to use credentials · Toolkits · Secrets

title: DeepWiki and Inventory
text: DeepWiki and Inventory are configured from Applications and, once set up, open at /deepwiki and /inventory . Visiting either route resolves your project's configured toolkit automatically: it opens directly if there is exactly one, offers a picker if there are several, or shows an empty state if none is configured yet. DeepWiki DeepWiki generates a searchable, AI authored wiki from a connected code repository — architecture summaries, source linked explanations, and a chat panel for asking questions about the codebase. Configuration: a code toolkit (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, or Azure DevOps Repos), an LLM model, a max token budget, and an embedding model. What you can do: Browse generated wiki pages and architecture diagrams. Ask questions in the wiki chat drawer, attaching specific wiki pages as context. Edit a generated page directly, or regenerate content for the connected repository. The wiki chat's history is read only — you cannot continue a previous session — and "attachments" in DeepWiki chat means attaching existing wiki pages as context, not uploading a file (tracked in 873). Inventory Inventory builds a knowledge graph of your codebase — components, dependencies, and ownership — so you can understand the code estate before planning a migration or refactor. Configuration: one or more repository toolkits (GitHub and Azure DevOps Repos by default) and the AI model settings used to build the graph. What you can do: Browse entities by name, type, layer, or source. Inspect a single component's properties and relationships. Ask questions about the ingested codebase in the Inventory chat panel. Review ingestion statistics for each connected source. Troubleshooting No toolkit of that type is configured yet in this project — configure one from Applications. Confirm the underlying repository toolkit's credentials are still valid, and check for a completion notification. Applications · Toolkits · Notifications

title: Help and support
text: Elitea offers two places to get help without leaving your work: the Help Center , a static hub of links your administrator configures, and the Support Assistant , a context aware AI chat widget. Help Center Select the ? button near the bottom of the sidebar to open the Help Center. Its default sections are Documentation , Release notes , Video library , Tutorials , and Interactive tours — each one links to whatever your administrator has configured under admin Configuration › Resources. Titles, descriptions, and links are fully customizable per deployment; a section with nothing configured shows "No links configured." When enabled, the header also shows the running platform version. If the Help Center looks empty, no links have been configured yet for this deployment — ask your administrator to add them. Support Assistant The Support Assistant is an optional, floating chat widget available from the sidebar when your administrator has turned it on. It tracks your current project, page, and any open entity (an agent, pipeline, toolkit, MCP, application, credential, or conversation), so its answers can be specific to what you're doing. What it can do: Answer questions in context, with full Markdown rendering — tables, code blocks, and Mermaid diagrams render as diagrams rather than raw text. Keep a history of your past conversations with it, reachable from the history icon in its header. Attach one file per message (image or document) by clicking the paperclip icon, dragging it onto the input, or pasting an image from the clipboard. Expand to a fullscreen view, and follow your light/dark theme automatically. Only a single file per message is supported today — drag and drop of multiple files, paste of multiple images, and an upload progress indicator are not available yet (tracked in 877). The Support Assistant authenticates using your personal access token. If your token is missing or expired, the widget fails to load or send messages — create or renew a token to fix it. Contact support Elitea does not ship a built in support ticket system. If something isn't covered by the Support Assistant or the documentation, reach out to your platform administrator directly, or use the Support Assistant itself for a first pass at a solution. Troubleshooting The feature is off for this deployment — ask your administrator to enable it in admin Features. Its backing agent may be misconfigured or missing valid credentials — this needs an administrator to check. Confirm the file is under the size limit and that you are attaching only one file per message. Settings › AI Providers · Personal tokens · Troubleshooting · FAQs

title: Internal tools
text: Internal tools are capabilities you turn on from Modules in chat or an agent's Tools section, without configuring an external toolkit. They come from a fixed platform catalogue ( features/agents/lib/internalTools.ts ) and are turned on per conversation or saved as an agent's default. Every internal tool on this page runs only when your deployment's worker is the Python worker. The Rust worker — Helm's default — skips each one with a logged warning and the agent still answers, just without that capability (tracked in 866). Ask your administrator which worker your deployment runs before relying on these in production. Turn a module on Select + in the chat toolbar → Modules , then toggle the tool on. The setting lasts for the conversation. Open the agent, find Modules under Tools (select Show all if it is collapsed), toggle the tool, and Save . New conversations with that agent turn it on by default. Image creation Generates images from a text prompt and shows them inline, using an image generation model configured in AI Providers . Generated images are saved automatically to the project's attachments bucket, where you can also download or delete them later from Artifacts. Data analysis Runs pandas style analysis over a file you upload to the conversation — summaries, filtering, aggregation, and chart generation — driven entirely by natural language requests. Upload the file first, then ask for the analysis; generated charts and exported files are saved back to the conversation. For datasets larger than about 100 MB, or analysis needing custom code, use a Python based toolkit or a pipeline Code node instead. Planner Lets an agent create, prioritize, and track tasks directly from natural language during a conversation — for example, "create a high priority task to review contracts by Friday." Tasks carry a title, priority, due date, and status, and are scoped to the conversation that created them: deleting or clearing the conversation removes its tasks too. Swarm mode Turns a set of agents into peers that can hand off control to one another mid conversation, all sharing the same conversation history. The agent the user addresses is simply the default entry point; any peer can transfer to any other with a transfer to tool, and each hand off's task argument must be fully self contained — the receiving agent gets no other context. Swarm enabled agents cannot themselves be added as a child of another swarm agent. Smart tools selection Reduces token usage when an agent has many toolkits configured by binding only two meta tools ( get tool schema , invoke tool ) instead of every individual tool definition, loading real tool schemas on demand. Turn it on once a conversation or agent uses five or more toolkits — the more toolkits, the larger the savings. Troubleshooting Confirm the deployment's worker is Python, not Rust — the Rust worker silently skips every module on this page. No image generation model is configured for the project yet — add one in AI Providers. No module is available for the project at all — ask your administrator to configure at least one provider or toolkit. Chat: Modules · Agents: Modules · Elitea MCP tools · Attach files

title: Platform overview
text: Every menu in Elitea shares the same shell: a sidebar for navigation, a project selector, and a consistent set of list, search, and organization controls. This page covers what is common; each menu's own page covers what is specific to it. Sidebar The sidebar gives you access to every menu: Chat — conversations with models, agents, pipelines, toolkits, and MCP servers. Agents , Pipelines , Skills — the entities you build and manage. Toolkits — integrations with external services, plus MCP servers when your administrator has turned on MCP menu exposure. Apps — installed applications (DeepWiki, Inventory) and the catalog of applications you can request access to. Credentials , Artifacts — supporting resources: authentication and file storage. Catalog — the shared library of published agents and skills. Settings — project and personal configuration. At the bottom of the sidebar you'll also find a ? Help Center button, a notification bell, and your user profile. Project selector Use the project selector at the top of the sidebar to switch between your personal project — visible only to you — and any team projects you belong to, where entities are shared and collaboratively managed according to each member's role. Common list controls Most menus (Agents, Pipelines, Skills, Toolkits, Credentials) share the same dashboard pattern: Card view and table view , toggled from the top of the list. A search box scoped to the current menu — search does not span menus. Tag filters to narrow the list by category. Pinning — pin an item to keep it at the top of its list. Sorting (table view) by name, created date, type, or author. What's next Start with the menu you need: Conversations and participants. Build and run agents. Multi step workflows. Reusable instruction sets. External integrations and MCP servers. Deployable, focused solutions. Authentication for integrations. Shared file storage. Published agents and skills. For definitions of terms used across these menus, see the Glossary.

title: Pipelines
text: A pipeline is a visual, multi step workflow. Where an agent handles one task end to end, a pipeline breaks a process into nodes — agent calls, toolkit actions, decisions, and state updates — and connects them into a repeatable sequence. Create a pipeline Creation is two phases. First, fill in Name , Description , and optionally tags, a welcome message, conversation starters, and a step limit (default 25), then select Save — this creates the pipeline's base version. Saving unlocks the second phase: a three column editor with the configuration form on the left, the Flow/YAML editor in the center, and a live test chat on the right. Attach toolkits, agents, MCPs, and nested pipelines In Tools , use +Toolkit , +MCP , +Agent , and +Pipeline to attach existing resources for the workflow to call. This section only appears after the first save. State Every pipeline starts with two built in state variables: inputs (the triggering input) and messages (the conversation history). Add your own under State with a name and optional default value, then reference them in any node as {{state.variable name}} . State Modifier nodes read and write state during execution. Design the workflow Toggle between Flow and YAML at the top of the center panel. Add a node with + , choose its type, and connect nodes by dragging between their connection points. See Flow editor and the pipeline node reference for what each node type does and which ones the runtime actually executes. Edit the same workflow as YAML for advanced control, bulk changes, or replicating an existing pipeline. See YAML editor. File attachments Turn on Attachments in Modules to let users upload files in a pipeline conversation. Elitea adds an input attachments state variable automatically (and removes it if you turn attachments off) and injects a file storage toolkit at execution time — no manual toolkit setup needed. Attachments require a default vector storage and embedding model configured for the project. Test and execute The embedded chat panel lets you pick a model, adjust its settings, and run the pipeline interactively. Each execution is captured as a pipeline run with its inputs, outputs, and state changes; when context management is on, a Context Budget widget tracks token usage during the run. See Pipeline runs. Versions, publishing, export, and fork Pipelines version, publish, export/import, and fork the same way agents do — select Save As Version to branch, use the version dropdown to switch, and reach Export , Fork , and Publish from the toolbar's overflow menu. See Entity versioning, Import/export, and Forking. Troubleshooting Check that every node has its required tools and credentials configured, and that connections between nodes are complete. Verify credentials and network access for the external service that node calls. Confirm the receiving node's task field actually references the sending node's output variable — the input space listing organizes variables but does not pass them automatically. Pipeline overview · Pipeline structure · Credentials · Toolkits

title: AI Providers
text: AI Providers is where a project registers the models and storage it uses, and picks defaults for each category. Settings here apply at the project level for every member. Categories Language models, with Default, High tier, and Low tier selections. Used for indexing and semantic search. Where embeddings are stored (PGVector). Powers the Image creation module in chat. Server side voice input. Server side spoken playback. Each category shows its configured models as cards with a provider icon, name, and a badge for Default, High tier, or Low tier. Select a card to edit it, if your role allows. Add a model or credential Choose a provider — OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Anthropic, Amazon Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, Ollama, vLLM, or EPAM AI Dial — and provide its endpoint and key. One credential can back several models. Select + , choose the model category, and fill in a display name, the exact provider model identifier, and — for LLMs — context window, max output tokens, and whether it supports reasoning or vision. Use the category's dropdowns to make the new configuration the project default, or the high tier / low tier choice. The Name field must be the provider's own model identifier (or Azure deployment name) — not a display label. Refer to your provider's model list if a connection or generation fails. When an OpenAI or Anthropic model configuration uses AI Dial credentials, leave Supports Reasoning off — turning it on breaks connection validation for that combination. Speech recognition and text to speech fallbacks If no ASR model is configured, voice input falls back to the browser's Web Speech API; if no TTS model is configured, playback falls back to the browser's SpeechSynthesis API. Elitea determines ASR mode from the model name — whisper or transcribe selects batch transcription; anything else uses realtime streaming. Troubleshooting Confirm the model name matches the provider's identifier exactly and that your credential has access to it. Recheck the API key or token for typos or expiry, and confirm the endpoint URL is correct for your provider. Confirm a default ASR or TTS model is actually selected in this page, not just configured. Credentials · Project settings · Voice

title: Analytics and usage
text: Analytics and Usage give you two views of the same underlying activity: Analytics is about understanding how the project is used; Usage is about tracking spend against a budget. Analytics Settings › Analytics is available to any project member and requires the analytics enabled admin flag. Data is scoped to the currently selected project and refreshed from the API, cached for a few minutes. Choose a date range with the quick presets (Last 24h/7d/30d/90d) or custom From/To pickers, then switch between tabs: Team size, AI adoption, LLM calls, tool runs, and the top adopters. Estimated LLM spend by day, by user, and by model. Input, output, and cache token usage by day, user, and model. Run counts, latency, and errors per agent or pipeline. Call counts, latency, and errors per tool. Per user activity, adoption, and the tools and agents they used. Request volume, error rates, and latency by event type. Select Export to Excel to download all tabs for the selected range as a single workbook. Costs and tokens break down by user and by model, and agent/pipeline analytics break down runs, latency, and errors per agent — but cost itself is never attributed to a specific agent or tool (tracked in 875). Usage Settings › Usage requires the cost budgets enabled admin flag and shows spend against the current monthly billing period for platform shared models only — models configured with your own provider credentials are billed by that provider and are not included. In a personal project the project budget is your own budget, so there is no tab switcher. In a team project, switch between: Whole project — total spend, a usage meter against the effective limit, daily usage, usage by model, and a Members table showing each member's own spend against their own limit. My usage — the same panels scoped to you alone. A warning banner appears as usage approaches its limit; once the limit is reached, requests to platform shared models are refused until the limit increases or the period resets. Select the export button to download usage data as an Excel file. Troubleshooting The relevant admin flag ( analytics enabled or cost budgets enabled ) is off for this deployment — ask your administrator. API results are cached briefly; wait a moment or select Refresh. Your project or personal budget for shared models has been reached for the current period — wait for the reset or ask an administrator to raise the limit. Admin: Budgets and governance · Project settings

title: Memory
text: Settings › Memory controls how much conversation history is kept and how it is managed as a conversation grows — not a persistent, cross conversation memory. A "Coming soon" placeholder for persistent, cross conversation recall exists in Profile, but it is not implemented — this Memory page is context window management only (tracked in 870). Context management Turn context management on to have Elitea automatically manage history as it approaches a model's token limit. Max Context Tokens (default 64,000) — the ceiling for conversation history sent per request. Preserve Recent Messages (default 5) — the number of most recent messages always kept, regardless of the token ceiling. Context editing When context management is on, context editing clears older tool outputs from the sent history while keeping recent results, reducing token usage without losing recent detail. Automatic summarization With context management on, turn on summarization to have Elitea condense older messages into a summary once the conversation grows past a threshold, instead of dropping them outright. Summarization instructions — free text guiding style and focus of the generated summary. Target Summary Tokens (default 4,096) — the target length for each generated summary. Summarization only runs while context management is turned on — turning context management off disables summarization too, even if its own toggle is still on. How settings apply All Memory settings apply to every new conversation you start in Chat, Agents, and Pipelines. Existing conversations, and conversations started by other users, keep their own settings. Troubleshooting Settings auto save on blur or on toggle — watch for a "Settings saved successfully" confirmation, and check numeric fields are within their valid range. Confirm context management is turned on — summarization is inactive whenever it is off. Context management · Chat

title: Notifications
text: Elitea delivers real time notifications over a live connection for events like publish decisions, mentions, budget thresholds, and expiring tokens. Quick popover Select the bell icon in the sidebar for a fast, unread only view: up to 5 items, with Mark as read on hover and Mark all as read / View all in the footer. Notifications Center Settings › Notifications shows every notification, read and unread, with search by message text, sortable Type and Date & Time columns, and bulk Mark as read , Mark as unread , and Delete actions. What triggers a notification | Event | What it means | | | | | Publish approved / rejected | Your published agent or skill version was reviewed. | | Mentioned or added to a conversation | A teammate @mentioned you or added you to a conversation. | | Index created, reindexed, or failed | A toolkit index finished or failed. | | Bucket expiration warning | Files in an artifact bucket will be deleted within 24 hours under its retention policy. | | Personal access token expiring | A token will stop working within 24 hours. | | Project or member budget threshold / limit reached | Shared model spend is near or at its monthly limit. | Several of these link straight to the relevant page — for example, an expiring token notification opens Settings › Personal Tokens, and a budget notification opens Settings › Usage. Troubleshooting Opening the popover does not mark items read automatically — use Mark as read or Mark all as read explicitly. Some links (for example, a mention) open the exact conversation and message; others open a settings page scoped to the relevant project. Personal tokens · Analytics and usage · Artifacts

title: Personal settings
text: Personal settings apply to you across every project — they never affect what your teammates see. Profile Settings › Profile shows your full name, email, user ID, and last login, and is where you sign out of Elitea. Preferences Settings › Preferences covers three areas: General — your theme: Dark, Light, or System. Voice personalization — your default text to speech voice, speed, and volume, with a preview button. Uses your project's configured server side voice model when available, otherwise your browser's built in voices. Sound notifications — whether Elitea plays a completion sound when a task finishes, and at what volume. AI Personality Settings › AI Personality sets the default communication style and any standing instructions applied to every new conversation you start. Default Personality — pick from Generic, QA, Nerdy, Quirky, Cynical, None (no personality overlay), or Bare (no Elitea identity at all, only your instructions). User Instructions — free text guidance (communication preferences, technical requirements, output format) that applies automatically to new conversations, agents, and pipelines. Settings save automatically as you edit; only new conversations pick up a change — existing ones keep what they started with. Start with the default persona and no instructions, use it for a few conversations, then adjust one setting at a time based on what you notice. Troubleshooting Confirm you are testing in a brand new conversation — existing conversations keep their original settings. Personality shapes tone and approach, not factual correctness — it is most visible in open ended or creative requests, not factual lookups. Memory · Chat

title: Personal tokens
text: A personal access token (PAT) authenticates API calls and IDE integrations as you, without using your password. Settings › Personal Tokens is where you create, inspect, and revoke them. Generate a token Select + . Give it a descriptive name and choose Never, or a number of days, weeks, hours, or minutes. The full token is shown only once — copy it immediately. It cannot be retrieved again after you close the dialog. Use "Never" only for personal development — set an expiration for anything used in a shared or production context. Manage tokens The table shows each token's last 4 characters value and an expiration status (a warning icon appears within 7 days of expiry). Select the preview icon to see ready made VS Code ( settings.json ) or JetBrains ( alita.xml ) configuration snippets for that token, copy or download them, or delete a token you no longer need. Troubleshooting It cannot be shown again — delete it and generate a new one. They only appear once a model configuration is selected and you are outside the Public project. Check whether its token expired; expired tokens stop authenticating immediately. Support Assistant · API and MCP endpoints

title: Project settings
text: Project settings cover the parts of a project every member shares: its identity, its background context, its secrets, and who belongs to it. General Settings › General shows the project's icon, name, and teammate count (hidden for the Public project), plus connection details for OpenAI compatible clients — an OpenAI BaseURL , server URL, and project ID you can copy for external tooling. A Default Modules section lets you turn modules (image creation, data analysis, planner, Python sandbox, smart tools selection, swarm mode, and more) on or off by default for chats and agents project wide; members can still override the default per conversation. Project Context Project Context is a background document — up to 2,500 characters of Markdown — that Elitea applies silently to every AI interaction in the project: domain, terminology, workflows, and constraints the model should always know. It is visible only in the Public project. Select Create to write it manually, or Build with AI to generate a first draft from a plain language description. Use Edit with AI to describe a change and review a side by side diff before it saves. Turning Project Context off preserves its content — you can turn it back on later. Individual agents can opt out with Ignore Project Context in their Advanced settings. Secrets Settings › Secrets is the project's vault for sensitive values — passwords, tokens, API keys — that credentials and toolkits reference instead of storing plain text. Only Admin, System, or Editor roles can access this section. Create a secret with a unique name (letters, digits, underscores only) and a value; the name cannot change afterward. Hide removes a secret from the UI and from future selection, while credentials already using it keep working. Delete removes it permanently — any credential using it fails authentication immediately. Every mutation is applied under a row lock, so two people editing the same secret at once no longer clobber each other's change. Users Settings › Users lists project members with their role and last login; it is hidden for a personal project. Only Admin can invite, edit roles for, or remove members. Select + Invite users , enter one or more email addresses (comma separated), and pick one or more roles. Edit a single user's roles, or select several and batch edit them together. Delete a user individually or in a batch, with confirmation. Available roles are System, Admin, Editor, Viewer, and Monitor; a user can hold more than one. Troubleshooting It only appears in the Public project, and requires view permission. Your role does not include access — ask a project admin. Recreate the secret under the same name, or update the credential to a new one. AI Providers · Credentials · Agents

title: Settings overview
text: Select Settings in the sidebar to manage Elitea at two levels: project settings, which apply to everyone in the current project, and personal settings, which apply only to you across every project. Project settings General info, project context, secrets, and users. Models, embeddings, vector storage, and AI credentials. Adoption, cost, and health metrics; budget consumption. Some project sections only appear in specific contexts: Project Context , Prompts , and Environment are visible only in the Public project; Users is hidden in a personal project; Analytics requires the analytics enabled admin flag and Usage requires cost budgets enabled . Personal settings Profile, preferences, and AI personality. Context window management for new conversations. API and IDE access tokens. Your notification history and preferences. Your role and permissions determine what you can view or edit within each section — some, like Secrets and Users, are restricted to Admin, System, or Editor roles. For definitions of roles and permissions, see the Glossary.

title: Skills
text: A skill is a focused, reusable instruction set — write it once in Markdown, attach it to as many agents as you need, and invoke it mid conversation with ~skill name . Skills are available in team and personal projects only; the Skills menu is hidden when the Public project is selected. Create a skill Select + in the sidebar, or Create from the Skills page, and choose Skill. Give it a Name (lowercase letters, digits, and hyphens only, no leading/trailing hyphen, 64 characters max, and it must not contain "claude" or "anthropic"), a Description , and optional tags. Enter the skill's instructions in the Markdown editor, up to 5,000 characters. Toggle Edit/Preview to check formatting. The skill opens with a test chat panel on the right so you can verify its behavior before attaching it to any agent. Select Generate with AI in the General section to describe what the skill should do in plain language and get a drafted name, description, and instructions to review before saving. Test a skill The right hand test chat is ephemeral — it is not saved and clears when you leave the page. Pick a model and adjust its settings the same way you would in a normal conversation, including voice input and playback if configured for the project. Versions Skills support named versions alongside the always present base version. Use Save As Version to create one — base is reserved and duplicate names are rejected. Set any version as the default from the overflow menu; you cannot delete the default or base version. Unlike agents and pipelines, skills have no version comparison or rollback view — only a flat list of named versions (tracked in 874). Export, import, fork, and publish Export downloads the current version as a .md file; Import on the Skills page uploads one back (always as a new base version, regardless of the version it was exported from). Fork copies a skill version into a project you choose. Publish submits a version to Catalog; Unpublish removes it. See Skill publishing. Attach a skill to an agent Open the agent, scroll to its Skills section, and select + Skill to search and attach — up to five skills per agent version. Each attachment uses the skill's base version by default; select the version name on the card to switch. Attaching requires the agent to be saved first. Use a skill in chat In a conversation with an agent that has skills attached, type ~ to open a picker of that agent's skills, then select one to invoke its instructions for that turn. Delete a skill Deleting a skill removes it from every agent it is attached to. Confirm by typing the skill's name in the delete dialog. Troubleshooting You are in the Public project — switch to a team or personal project. Check the character limits and validation rules on Name, Description, and Instructions, and confirm something actually changed since the last save. Save the agent first, or check whether it already has five skills attached. The current agent has no skills attached yet — attach one and start a new conversation. Agents · Entity versioning · Import/export · Catalog

title: Toolkits
text: A toolkit is a configured integration with an external service, or with an Elitea native capability, that gives agents and pipelines the ability to act. Elitea serves 52 toolkit types; see the full toolkit catalogue for the list, categories, and which deployment worker runs each one. Create a toolkit Select + Toolkit from the Toolkits page, or /toolkits/create from anywhere. Choose a type from the categorized tile grid, or search by name. Give it a Name and Description , select or create a Credential , and set any type specific parameters. For index capable types, optionally select a PGVector configuration and embedding model to turn on indexing. In Tools , turn on only the operations the toolkit needs — grouped as Read, Create & update, Delete, and Execute — then Save . Which toolkit types actually run depends on the worker your deployment uses. A type the current worker cannot build is served with its tile hidden rather than shown broken. Helm's default Rust worker hides 17 legacy toolkit types (tracked in 865); the compose/dev default Python worker fails to import 4 types — Google Places, Rally, ServiceNow, and Slack (tracked in 869). Check the toolkit catalogue for the exact list per worker. Advanced users can switch a toolkit's configuration to Raw JSON editing from the form/JSON toggle. Organize with folders The Folders panel on the right groups toolkits for easier navigation. Create a folder with + Folder , then move a toolkit into it from the folder icon on its card (hover to reveal it). Removing a toolkit from a folder does not delete it — it just returns to the main list. Pin frequently used folders from their three dot menu. Shared credentials in team projects If a toolkit uses a shared credential that each team member must supply individually, a Credential setup required banner appears on its card until you create the matching private credential. Changing a shared credential can make the toolkit stop working for teammates who have not configured their own — consider the impact before doing so. Test a toolkit Select Test on a toolkit's detail page to open a dedicated test view: pick a tool, a model, and any required parameters, then run it and review the result. See Test toolkit tools. Indexing Toolkit types that carry an index data tool (Artifact, the ADO family, Bitbucket, Confluence, Figma, GitHub, GitLab, Jira, QTest, SharePoint, TestRail, XRAY Cloud, and the Zephyr family) show an Indexes panel once PGVector and an embedding model are configured and the Index data tool is turned on. Use it to create, reindex, or delete indexes. See Indexing overview. MCP servers MCP servers extend agents, pipelines, and conversations with tools from an external Model Context Protocol server, configured the same way as a toolkit. The MCPs menu is shown when your administrator has turned on MCP menu exposure. Remote MCP — an HTTP/HTTPS based server. Provide its URL and authentication (a bearer token, OAuth client credentials, or custom headers), then load and select its tools. Pre built MCP servers — administrator curated connections your project can enable directly. See Pre built MCP servers. A connection shows Connected or Disconnected on its card. Elitea's own MCP connections run over streamable HTTP only — there is no local, STDIO based MCP server or client in the platform. Enable Make tools available by MCP on a toolkit's Tools section to expose its selected tools to external MCP clients through Elitea's own MCP server. See Make tools available by MCP. Use toolkits and MCPs Attach a toolkit or MCP from an agent's or pipeline's Tools section, or add it as a participant directly in a conversation. Troubleshooting Verify the selected credential and any required URL or project identifier, and confirm the target service is reachable. The running worker may not support that type — check the toolkit catalogue, or ask your administrator whether the type is restricted for this project. Confirm the toolkit type supports indexing, that PGVector and an embedding model are configured in AI Providers, and that Index data is turned on in Tools. For a Remote MCP, verify the server URL is reachable and its authentication has not expired. Credentials · How to use credentials · Webhooks and triggers · Toolkit catalogue

title: Pipeline node reference
text: The Flow editor's Add node menu offers more node types than the runtime compiler admits. This page lists both, plus the rules for node ids and state. Node types These are the only node types the pipeline compiler accepts and will actually run: decision · agent · toolkit · mcp · hitl · llm · printer · router · state modifier See the node type guides: interaction nodes, execution nodes, and control flow nodes (which also covers state modifier and printer, the utility nodes). tool , pipeline , function , loop , loop from tool , and condition still appear in some existing flows for backward compatibility, but the compiler has no execution arm for them — their editor tooltips still point at older migration material that this documentation set does not carry forward. Rebuild any flow that still uses one of these with an admitted node type instead. code and custom render in the editor but have no compiler arm either, so the Add node menu withholds them. END marks a pipeline's completion point; ghost and defaultType are internal placeholders you will not select directly. Node id rules A node id must match ^[A Za z0 9 .: ]+$ and be 128 bytes or fewer. Avoid spaces or other punctuation — a node id containing a space is a common cause of a pipeline that fails to save or compile. Reserved state keys Do not use these names for your own state variables — the runtime writes to them directly: elitea hitl resume v1 · elitea tool resume v1 · elitea llm tool resume v1 · elitea pipeline node event scope v1 · elitea application task v1 · elitea application messages v1 · elitea application result v1 · elitea subgraph result v1 · output · result · router output · elitea response · printer output · state types · context info · hitl decisions · hitl interrupt · parallel tasks · pipeline blocked · session id · thread id · execution finished · chat history input and messages are built into every pipeline (see State) but are not on the reserved list — you can still read them, just don't redefine them with a conflicting shape. Troubleshooting It is likely one of the render only/deprecated types. Replace it with the closest runtime admitted type — for example, replace tool with toolkit , and function with code 's admitted successor once available, or an llm / toolkit node. Check the id against the ^[A Za z0 9 .: ]+$ pattern and the 128 byte limit — spaces are the most common cause. Confirm its name is not one of the reserved keys above; pick a different name if it collides. Pipelines · Pipeline structure · Flow editor · YAML editor

title: Frequently asked questions
text: Your personal project is visible only to you — a sandbox for experimenting. A team project shares its agents, pipelines, toolkits, and conversations with every member, according to their role. Switch between them with the project selector at the top of the sidebar. Skills are hidden when the Public project is selected. Switch to a team or personal project. Only if the agent uses a toolkit that requires one. A plain agent with no toolkits needs only a model — configured once for the whole project in AI Providers. Yes, as long as they were saved as a version. Use the version dropdown on the agent to switch to an earlier version, or export a version as a backup file. It stops working immediately. Elitea shows the same "unavailable" message whether a link was revoked, expired, or never valid, so a recipient cannot tell which case applies. Its model likely hit the configured Max Completion Tokens limit. Increase it in the agent's model settings — and check any nested agents' limits too. See Troubleshooting. Yes — one credential can back several toolkits and agents. See Credentials. Which toolkit types are available depends on the worker your deployment runs, and on any restriction your administrator applied. See the toolkit catalogue. No — deleting a secret is permanent, and every credential referencing it fails authentication immediately. Consider hiding a secret first if you only want to stop new usage while confirming nothing still depends on it. See Troubleshooting for error message specific fixes, or reach your platform administrator through Help and support.

title: Troubleshooting
text: Start with the health checklist for a fast overall check, then use the category sections below for a specific error message. Quick health checklist Green dot on the Elitea logo = connected. Red = check your network. You can create the entities your role should allow (agents, toolkits, credentials). Test Connection on a credential returns success. Visible on a toolkit only once PGVector, an embedding model, and the Index data tool are all configured. If any of these fail, fix that first — most downstream errors trace back to one of them. Agent and LLM issues The model hit its Max Completion Tokens limit. Increase the value in the agent's model settings; check nested agents too if the issue appears mid chain. The message or instructions triggered the provider's safety mechanism. Avoid sensitive topics and phrasing that reads like a prompt injection attempt (for example, "ignore user input"); state the purpose of any such instruction clearly. Shared models on your deployment share per second/minute/day limits across every user. Wait and retry, or switch models. Input plus history exceeded the model's context window. Reduce the input, turn on context management, or index the source instead of pasting it directly. Turn on Structured Output when an LLM node has more than one output variable, and instruct the model to return JSON keyed by your variable names. Pipeline configuration issues Every pipeline needs one designated starting node — open the node's three dot menu and select Entry Point . A node (Agent, Decision, Router, and others) has an empty Task field — required fields must be filled before the pipeline can run. The task field must explicitly reference the variable, using an f string or the variable picker — listing a variable under Input alone does not pass it to the node automatically. A node has no agent or toolkit selected in its dropdown — select one. Toolkit and integration issues The connected account's token cannot see one or more items. Narrow the source with a filter (JQL for Jira, CQL for Confluence) and retry — items deleted mid run also surface this way. Recheck the credential's key or token for typos, extra whitespace, or expiry, and confirm the authentication method (basic vs. bearer) matches what the target service expects. Its configuration has a Limit field capping results per request — raise it in the toolkit's configuration. A required field is empty after an import or an update to the toolkit's schema — review every configuration section, including advanced settings, and fill anything marked required. MCP issues For a Remote MCP, verify the server URL is reachable and its authentication has not expired. Elitea's MCP connections are HTTP only — there is no local, STDIO based server or client to run first. Reload the MCP's configuration page, and confirm the server actually exposes tools once connected. Look at the end of the message for the real cause — one failure can cascade into another. For pipelines, the error usually names the node ("During task with name 'Agent1'"); open that node's configuration first. Operator checks Two different things answer "is the platform healthy," at two different levels. Infrastructure liveness and readiness elitea main exposes unauthenticated health endpoints for your load balancer, orchestrator, or uptime check: GET /healthz — liveness. Answers once the process is up; it does not check dependencies. GET /readyz — readiness. Checks the dependencies the service actually needs (for example, the database) and reports which one failed if it is not ready. Point your platform's health probe (Kubernetes liveness/readiness probe, or an external uptime monitor) at these rather than at an authenticated API route. The Health tab (application level) Inside the app, Settings › Analytics › Health (gated by the analytics enabled admin flag — see Features and configuration) reports on the LLM gateway path specifically: Error codes — a table of upstream and gateway error codes seen recently, by count. This reads the gateway's per request log, not the billing ledger, so a call that was refused by a budget, rejected by policy, or failed upstream shows up here even though it never generated a billed event. Model health — which configured models are currently returning errors, and how often. Activity trend — a day by day chart of request volume. If nothing appears on this tab, check the analytics enabled flag before assuming the platform is idle — the tab is gated off entirely rather than shown empty when the flag is off. Use the infrastructure endpoints to answer "is the service up," and the Health tab to answer "are calls through the LLM gateway succeeding." Check the FAQs, or reach your platform administrator through Help and support.

title: What's new
text: Elitea ships frequent, small releases. This page summarizes the most recent user visible changes; it is not a full changelog. Client deployment readiness You can now configure a fresh deployment entirely from the UI — set the first global administrators, create a project, and add an AI provider — without running SQL by hand. Platform parity wave A broad pass closed gaps across several areas at once: issue triage fixes, the toolkit catalogue, the support assistant bot, Inventory, and wiki source connections all received fixes and completions. Post release fixes Follow up fixes landed for session handling, admin 403 errors, invite links, the maintenance splash screen, voice configuration, artifact bucket access control lists, and the admin Tasks page. The secrets vault also gained write locking, so concurrent edits to the same secret no longer overwrite each other silently. Detailed release notes are published as GitHub releases on the platform repository. This page lists only the changes that affect what you see or do in the product.
